newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says will sign Turkey gas deal in July. [CORRECTED 09:27 GMT 06/04]
newsitem.headline: Iraq says will sign Turkey gas deal in July. [CORRECTED 09:27 GMT 06/04]

text.p: Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said in remarks published on Saturday that Iraq would soon sign a 20-year contract in July to sell Iraqi gas to neighbouring Turkey.

"The next month of July will witness the signing of the first contract to sell Iraqi gas to Turkey. The contract will cover twenty years," the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya quoted Rasheed as saying.
Under the deal the two countries would construct a 1,300 km (corrects from 300 km) long gas pipeline at a cost of $2.5 billion. It would be capable of carrying 10 billion cubic feet of gas a year.
"The technical sides in the two countries have taken important steps to complete the practical measures needed for the implementation," said the minister.
He said the final details of the deal would be set during a visit to Baghdad by Turkish Energy Minister Recai Kutan at the end of April.
Iraq is under stringent U.N. trade sanctions imposed after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. But the U.N. has allowed it to sell limited oil since last December to pay for urgent needs.
The minister did no say when the deal would go into effect.

The United States has voiced its concerns about other deals signed by Turkey with countries in the region. The State Department said on Friday it was seeking details of a contract awarded by Turkey this week for part of a natural gas pipeline link with Iran to see if the agreement violated U.S. law.

Most of Iraq's gas production consists solely of associated gas dissolved in oil and contained in oilfield gas gaps. But Iraq boasts several gasfields among them Al-Anfal which came on stream in May 1990 at a rate of 200 million cubic feet a day.
Official estimates put proven gas reserves at more than 3,115 billion cubic metres in 1989.
Turkey is trying to secure as many deals as possible under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.

Jumhouriya quoted Turkish State Minister Ahmet Cemil Tunc, who ended a Baghdad visit on Thursday, as saying his country had signed deals worth $70 million with Iraq for the supply of humanitarian goods under the oil deal.
About 60 percent of Iraq's partial oil sales under its deal with the U.N. go through its pipelines via Turkey.
